release_review.summary: Redeven v0.11.0 separates Connect, Workspace, and Runtime management authority, moves managed Runtime operations to the durable Gateway v2 supervisor, and introduces Runtime Service v2 lifecycle fencing at compatibility epoch 9 without making ordinary Runtime access depend on Gateway.
checked_surfaces: Redeven consumes published github.com/floegence/floret/v4 v4.0.12 with GOWORK=off and exact module checksums; canonical queue and interaction acceptance precedes visible success, unknown effect retries claim the stable source once, delete and shutdown fence active subtrees and effect dispatch, migration v2 through v5 remains atomic and fail-closed, ordered views stay monotonic across live updates and restart, and no replace, go.work, sibling source path, copied contract, internal import, or Floret schema access exists
Floret ThreadService is the only lifecycle boundary for View, Send, Respond, Cancel, Retry, RetryEffect, PromoteQueued, and Subscribe
Each Floret thread has one in-memory ThreadRuntime owner; its canonical journal is the only durable lifecycle fact source
Redeven persists only product settings, authorization audit, uploads, read state, and the contiguous v1-to-v2 migration import boundary
Redeven handlers authorize and map typed requests without admission receipts, authority barriers, recovery handles, or projection mirrors
Flower uses one workspace SSE, summary/detail-separated ThreadCache, ComposerDraftStore, short-lived IndexedDB TransportOutbox, and LiveTransport
Thread selection never owns execution or reconnects transport; summary updates never overwrite typed detail
Unknown irreversible tool effects are not replayed automatically and remain recoverable only from their original tool row

Redeven consumes only published Flowersec Go and Core v2.5.2 plus Floe Webapp v0.41.4, with exact module checksums, one resolved npm version across Desktop, Env App, and Code App, and no replace, file, link, workspace, portal, sibling checkout, private import, or copied transport implementation

Local UI and the trusted Desktop bridge use Flowersec Acceptor sessions with exact loopback Host and Origin admission, one-shot artifacts, isolated concurrent windows, explicit terminal failure, and cleanup of pending authorization, handlers, sessions, and notification sinks

Each remote or local accepted session registers the final Flowersec SessionHandlers, RPC, ByteStream, and terminal/live_v1 boundaries directly; outbound terminal notification sinks attach to the established Flowersec RPC peer and detach idempotently when that session ends

Desktop attach and start, Local UI health, startup reports, sys.ping, Env App maintenance, SSH runtime bootstrap, public WSS, loopback direct WebSocket, terminal history recovery, and consecutive Desktop bridge sessions remain covered by the exact-main integration and focused transport contracts

Flowersec ConnectionController remains the only reconnect owner; secure-session retry uses Floe Webapp replaceConnection so an old asynchronous close cannot overwrite a new controller generation, while Redeven supplies artifact acquisition, authorization, permissions, product RPC handlers, and post-session business recovery without a second reconnect state machine or alternate carrier path
Runtime Service protocol_version is redeven-runtime-v2 at compatibility_epoch 9; lifecycle incompatibility disables Runtime management without changing authorized Connect and Workspace paths
Gateway and Runtime component versions are independent and compatibility is decided by signed digest, protocol, epoch, and capability facts
